Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the visible text of the Browser pane's page (article/main content first, falls back to body innerText).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes — edit source code instead.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description: Action to perform (only `javascript_exec` is supported).

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. Return values are serialized as JSON.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__navigate
tools.description: Navigate the Browser pane to a URL, or go "back"/"forward" in history. If the Browser pane isn't open yet, this opens it at the URL (no dev server needed).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

Contents of /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/AGENTS.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Branches

- `jusprin-dev` is the development branch. Start each change on a new branch from it and land the change there. It began at `975c703f08`, the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and contains the earlier development branches `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those.
- `main` is the stable branch and GitHub's default branch: the repository's front page, its issue forms, and the workflows GitHub runs on a schedule come from it.
  - Never force-push `main`, so that people who cloned the repository never have to force-pull. Only in an extreme case with no other way out, and with Kenneth's yes, may an admin lift the GitHub protection that blocks force pushes and deletion.
  - For now `main` is also the release branch: it moves forward from `jusprin-dev` when a version is released, and releases are built from it. This may change if a separate release branch is added later.
- `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1, for fixes to that version only.
- `jusprin-v2-poc` holds the experiments described below.
- Take each OrcaSlicer release into `jusprin-dev` as `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` rule 10 describes.

## Releasing

`.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds a release into a draft on GitHub; its top comment says how to start it. It refuses the commit until it has all of these:

- The version, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`, above every released JusPrin version.
- The release notes, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`.
- The Sentry secrets: `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, the project the app sends error reports and crashes to, and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT`, which upload each build's debug files and the pages' source maps. A platform's build fails unless Sentry then holds debug information with file and line for the app's own code (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh`) and a source map for each page as built (`sentry_page_maps.sh` beside it); the nightly build checks the same.
- The guide, `docs/guide/`, checked for that version. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` on a built copy of the commit, fix every page it reports, and commit the pages with their pictures, skills and `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`, as `docs/guide/README.md` describes under "Before a release". That file names the version the check last passed for, not the commit. Ticking "Release without the guide check" on the workflow's Run workflow form skips this, and the draft's title then says so. A release started by pushing a `jusprin-release/` branch has no form, so it always needs the file.

## Error handling

Someone pastes a key from their own AI service, and the service refuses it because of a setting in their account. Only they can change that setting. Later the app loses a chat because of a mistake in our code. Only we can fix that. Every failure is like one of these: there is someone who can do something about it, and error handling is the work of getting the failure to them, in a form they can use.

A failure that is the person's has to reach them in words they can understand, saying truthfully where the problem lies and what to do next. When the other side, meaning the service, printer or system that refused, has already said this in words written for a person, show those words and say who said them, because it knows the situation better than a sentence we prepared. Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing share one sentence, since a second sentence tells them nothing more. Nothing is wrong with the app itself, so it carries on.

A failure that is ours has to reach us with everything the code knew, because we will have to find the cause. The person can do nothing with that detail. They need to know only that the fault is not theirs, and to have a way to send it to us. We write no code to deal with such a failure. Its cause is something we did not understand when we wrote the code, so any handling would be a guess, and a guess carries on in a state nobody can vouch for and hides the failure. The work stops.

Sending a failure to the wrong one is the mistake this section exists to prevent, and it can be made in both directions. Tell the person the service could not be reached when our server failed, and they check their network while we never hear of it. Tell them something went wrong on our side when their own account is out of credits, and they wait for us while our reports fill with things we cannot fix, until the ones we can fix are hard to see.

So look at the failure itself, with what the other side actually said, and work out whose it is. Usually it says. What we have prepared does not change the answer: a failure that is the person's stays theirs when nobody wrote a sentence for it. When it truly cannot be told, it comes to us, because a report we cannot use costs us one look, while a failure of ours that only the person saw is lost.

Sometimes that someone is neither the person nor us. A service the person chose, such as the AI service their own key is for, is down, overloaded or failing on its own side: whoever runs it can fix it, and nobody here can. The person still needs the truth, that the trouble is at that service and not with them or with JusPrin, so they stop looking for something to fix. It is not reported, because a report is for someone who can act on it. Behind a JusPrin account the AI service is ours, because we chose it and can change it, so its failures come to us.

A failure we know people will meet is part of the feature, and the feature is not finished until the person who meets it is told what to do. Every failure is also written to the log, whoever it goes to. The log is where we look when a report or a question sends us looking. It tells nobody anything by itself.

### In practice

- Whose a failure is depends on its cause, such as "out of credits" or "no network", both of them the person's. A status code, an exception type, or the way the failure arrives (an HTTP status, an event inside a reply) is not a cause.
- A branch for "anything else" decides for every failure nobody listed. A failure the other side says is the person's goes to the person, and one that cannot be told comes to us. One sentence there for failures with different owners is a guess.
- A sentence we write for the person needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message. Each has a test, and each time it is shown is counted. Showing the other side's own words needs no sentence of ours.
- A failure that is the person's, or that nobody here can fix, is handled with normal control flow, not exceptions, and is not reported.
- A failure that is ours gets one sentence, "Something went wrong on our side", and a way to report it. Do not sort such failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of one. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- A failure that is ours stops the work and travels up unchanged. Do not catch it, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Once it is clear that it is ours, or that it cannot be told whose it is, turn it into a thrown error on the spot and keep the other side's status, request id and error text.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports through `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`) and tells the person. No other code reports. In the code, a failure that comes to us is called unexpected, and any other is called expected.
- The report carries the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is ours.
- One exception to "the work stops" and "no other code reports": a tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, with no dialog, and for this kind of failure only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- Never record a failure as a success.

### Catching

- Catch a failure only when the code knows what it is and can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against this section. Of each failure the code decides on, with what the other side really says, it asks: whose is it, and does it reach them in a form they can use?
- To audit a commit range, use the `error-handling` skill (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`). To check production for a period, use the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise repository.

## Build Commands

Build the Release configuration unless asked otherwise.

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config Release --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config Release --target all --

# Windows
cmake --build . --config Release --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.
- Before building against a dependency folder built earlier, such as the main checkout's `deps/build/arm64`, run `scripts/deps_current.sh <folder>`. It rebuilds the libraries whose `deps/` recipe changed since that folder was built.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/`; see [tests/AGENTS.md](tests/AGENTS.md) for where a new test belongs and the conventions to follow.

```bash
cd build && ctest -C Release --output-on-failure    # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r -C Release       # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print -C Release
```

## Documentation

- Docs live in `docs/`; the high-level design of a subsystem goes in `docs/HLSD/<subsystem>.md`.
- Describe the design as it stands — what the subsystem does, why it exists, and the constraints that shape it. Not the route that got there: no phases, task lists, status markers, or "before/after this PR" framing.
- Planning and investigation output (brainstorms, superpowers design and plan docs) stays in `docs/superpowers/`, which is gitignored. Never commit it.
- Write a doc only when the design is not evident from the code, and when a change invalidates an existing one, update it in the same PR.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Include what you use: include the header for every symbol a file uses, and keep headers compilable on their own. Never rely on the precompiled header or a transitive include. The `clang-tidy` CI job enforces this on changed lines; run the same check locally with `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` (`scripts\run_clang_tidy.ps1` on Windows), which sets up everything it needs
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.
- Always use `SetSizerAndFit(sizer)` instead of `SetSizer(sizer)` on top level window. Unless `SetSizer` must be called before the full layout is built, call `sizer->SetSizeHints(window)` afterwards in this case.

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
- For profile changes (`resources/profiles/<Vendor>/**`), check that `version` in the sibling `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json` was bumped.
- For new or changed UI strings, check they follow [Writing translatable strings in the source](#writing-translatable-strings-in-the-source): no concatenated fragments, plural forms for counts, contexts for ambiguous words.
- For translation changes (`localization/i18n/**/*.po`), check that recurring terms match the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) for that language.

## Localization & translations

Catalogs live in `localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`; the template is `OrcaSlicer.pot`.
See the [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md) for the human-facing version of these principles.

### Writing translatable strings in the source

Translators see one msgid at a time and cannot change the code around it, so each message must be complete in a single msgid. Use the wrapper that fits instead of assembling text from pieces:

- **One msgid per sentence, with placeholders.** Never build a message by concatenating translated fragments (`_L("A") + name + _L(" is B")`) or by splicing a translated word such as `_L("left")` into another sentence: the translator can't reorder or inflect the parts. Write `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)`.
- **A count needs a plural form.** Don't write `file(s)` or leave a verb unchanged after a number. Use `_L_PLURAL("%1% object", "%1% objects", n)`. libslic3r has no plural lookup, so word the message so it doesn't depend on a count, or build it in the GUI.
- **An ambiguous word needs a context.** When a short string means different things in different places (verb or noun, a mode name, a CAD term), give each sense its own context with `_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`/`L_CONTEXT`. Keep the most common sense without a context so its existing translations stay valid.
- **Mark every user-visible string** (`_L`/`_u8L`, or `L` where it is translated later) and list new source files in `localization/i18n/list.txt`: files that aren't listed are never extracted.
- Add a `// TRN` comment above a new string whose meaning or placeholders aren't obvious.
- Never choose behavior by comparing translated text; compare ids or flags.

See `.claude/skills/orca-translations/references/source-audit.md` for the full checklist.

### Terminology

- Use the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) as the source of truth for recurring terms, so the same English term is always rendered the same way within a language, and terms that must stay in English (brand/product names, acronyms, materials, file formats, G-code tokens, macros/variables/identifiers) are not translated.
- If a term's established translation changes, update both the affected `.po` files and the glossary (`developer_reference/glossary/<lang>.tsv` in the wiki, then regenerate) so they stay in sync.
- Translate the *meaning*, not the words. Check what the string actually controls before translating it — English reuses one word for different things. `Flow ratio` (multiplier), `Flow Rate` (throughput) and `Flow Dynamics` (pressure compensation) are three different terms; `extruder` may mean the toolhead, the feeder motor, or the nozzle depending on the string.
- Reuse one template per recurring message shape (`Failed to connect to …`, `Are you sure you want to …?`), even where the English wording varies.

### Editing rules

- Only edit `msgstr` — **never** change `msgid`, and never "fix" wrong English in the translation alone. Report the source string instead.
- Preserve exactly: placeholders (`%s`, `%d`, `%1%`, `%zu`, `%%`), every `\n` (count *and* position, including leading/trailing), leading/trailing spaces, HTML tags, `℃`, and the file's encoding and line endings.
- **Never reorder positional arguments** in a `c-format` string. If the msgid is `%d` then `%s`, that order must hold — swapping them breaks at runtime.
- `msgctxt` separates homonyms — always read it. `Back`/`Camera View` is the rear view of the 3D navigator, while `Back`/`Navigation` is the go-back button; `Top` exists in the *Alignment*, *Layers* and *Camera View* senses.
- When a string needs disambiguating, add context in the source (`_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`), don't work around it in the translation.
- A literal `%` inside a string xgettext flagged `possible-c-format` will fail `msgfmt`. Fix it with a `// xgettext:no-c-format, no-boost-format` comment above the string in the source — do not mangle the translation or use `%%` in text that is never passed through printf.
- Plural entries: read `nplurals` from the catalog's `Plural-Forms` header (it is **not** always 2 — ja/ko/zh/th/vi use 1, ru/cs/pl/lt use 3, uk uses 4). Each form must be genuinely inflected for its quantity; repeating one sentence across all forms is a bug in Slavic/Baltic languages, though it is correct for Turkish and Hungarian.
- An entry whose `msgstr` equals its `msgid` is untranslated even though it is not empty; a plural entry with any empty form is likewise incomplete.
- Mark machine-produced translations with an `# AI Translated` translator comment. Don't add it to a human translation you didn't actually rewrite.
- When you can't be sure of a machine translation's meaning or UI wording, also add `# Needs human review: <what to check>`. Never use `fuzzy` for this — fuzzy entries are hidden from users.
- Don't reflow or re-wrap unrelated entries — keep the diff limited to the strings you changed.

### Verifying

- `scripts/run_gettext.bat --full` (Windows) regenerates the template, merges every catalog and compiles the `.mo` files. It must exit 0.
- Or check a single catalog with `msgfmt --check-format --check-header -o <out>.mo localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`. Without `--check-header`, msgfmt skips the placeholder check in plural forms.
- Fuzzy entries are not shown to users. If you correct one, clear its `fuzzy` flag, otherwise the fix never ships.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m -q --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

---
name: jusprin-release
description: Use when asked to make, prepare or start a new JusPrin release (a new version on GitHub), from choosing the commit range to the after-publish steps. Covers the version, release notes, server readiness, translations, the error-handling audit, tests, the guide check, moving main, the release workflow, testing the draft and what follows publishing. Not for JusPrin 1 (jusprin-v1) or OrcaSlicer's own releases.
---

# Making a JusPrin release

`.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds one commit into a draft
release. It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes, a guide
check and the Sentry secrets (see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not
run tests, check the server, check translations or audit error handling.
This skill covers all of it, in order.

## Kenneth decides these

Ask, and wait for his yes before each one. A yes covers that action only.

- The version, when he has not named it, and the release notes' wording.
- Deploying the server.
- Which error-handling findings must be fixed before the release.
- Taking in commits that landed on `jusprin-dev` after the range was fixed.
- Spending API money (say the cost).
- Every push, and moving `main`.
- Starting the release workflow.
- Downloading the draft's files.
- The Sentry values and read-only token for checking the draft.
- Posting anything on GitHub.

Never publish the draft: Kenneth does, by hand. Never force-push `main`.

## When something has to be fixed

A fix is its own commit on `jusprin-dev`, made in a worktree of its own from
`origin/jusprin-dev`, never in the release commit. Once it is pushed:

- **Before section 8 landed the release commit:** rebase your branch onto
  `origin/jusprin-dev`, record that as the new end of the range, and redo
  step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7.
- **After it landed:** keep the version. Redo step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7
  up to the fix, land what changed (section 8), move `main` and start the
  workflow again. A new run for the same version replaces the draft.

## Where each platform is tested

Every release is tested on all three platforms, twice: the test suites
(section 5) and the draft's own files (section 10). An untested platform
blocks the release.

- **macOS:** this computer.
- **Windows and Linux:** the two Google Cloud test VMs. How to reach, start,
  build on and run the app on each is in
  `<main checkout>/.claude/vm-harness/windows/README.md` and `…/linux/README.md`.
  That folder is local to this computer, never in the repository. Start a
  stopped VM, and stop it again when done. If a VM or that folder is
  missing, stop and tell Kenneth.

## 1. Set up

1. The main checkout (the folder holding `jusprin-dev`) must have no changed
   tracked files and no commits missing from `origin/jusprin-dev`. If it has
   any, list them for Kenneth and wait; never push, commit or discard them
   yourself. Untracked files are his working docs and do not block.
2. The range is the newest `jusprin/v*` tag to the current
   `origin/jusprin-dev`. Record that commit: every later step checks this
   range, and section 8 checks whether `jusprin-dev` moved.
3. Settle the version, then make a worktree at that commit under
   `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`, on branch `claude/release-<version>` (add a
   suffix if taken). Never name a branch `jusprin-release/...`: pushing one
   starts an unsigned release build.
4. Read every commit in the range for what a person would notice and the
   GitHub issues it fixes.

## 2. Version and release notes

1. `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`.
2. `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`, shaped like
   the previous one, for a person who prints. It becomes the draft's text on
   every workflow run, and an older app shows it under "Release notes" in
   Preferences › Updates. Check every on-screen label you quote against the
   source.
3. Anything new the app sends from the person's computer goes in the notes,
   with what it holds.

## 3. Server readiness

Every address the release calls must already answer on
`https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Many are joined from pieces, so list them from
the code that builds them and write out each full path:

```bash
git grep -n -E '"/(ent|o|accounts|jusprin)/|"/models"|ask_server\("' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*'
```

For example `ask_server("code/confirm", …)` is
`/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/code/confirm`, and the model list is the gateway's
address with its last part replaced by `/models`. A bare GET with no sign-in
or real data is enough: any 4xx answer except 404 means the address is there.

First GET a made-up address such as `/ent/jusprin/v2/no-such-address`: it
must answer 404. In maintenance mode the server answers 200 for every path,
and the check cannot tell anything apart; stop and tell Kenneth.

A missing address means the server change is not deployed. Find it in
tsd-enterprise (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`) and tell Kenneth,
along with any other server behavior the range relies on. Deploying is his
call.

## 4. Error-handling audit

Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
server changes, also audit tsd-enterprise's `web_ent/jusprin/` commits on
`master` since the previous tag's date (that repository has no release tags).
Report the findings and wait for Kenneth to say which must be fixed.

## 5. Tests

Build in your worktree in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
in `AGENTS.md`. Use CMake.app's cmake (Homebrew's fails to find Eigen3), node
on `PATH`, and absolute paths.

The app builds against the main checkout's dependency folder, which may
predate a dependency the range added or changed. Bring it up to date first:

```bash
<worktree>/scripts/deps_current.sh <main checkout>/deps/build/arm64
```

It compares the `deps/` recipe the folder was last built from with the
worktree's, and when they differ it rebuilds the libraries that changed. If
it says the main checkout's recipe differs from the worktree's, the main
checkout is not at the end of the range; stop and tell Kenneth.

```bash
cmake -S <worktree> -B <worktree>/build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<main checkout>/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
cmake --build <worktree>/build/arm64 --config Release --target tests/all jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs -- -j4
ctest --test-dir <worktree>/build/arm64/tests -C Release --output-on-failure -LE RequiresApp
```

`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` takes one path only. `tests/all` builds every test
program, including `shell_integration_harness` for the guide check.
`agent_live_tests` is built but never registered with ctest, since each run
is billed. Also run `npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.

- **Windows and Linux,** on the VMs, from a checkout of the end of the range:
  `build_win.bat -s --run-tests`, and `./build_linux.sh -st` then
  `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release --output-on-failure`, keeping the
  `RequiresApp` tests, which run only on Linux.
- **Prompt suites,** when the range changes text the model reads: run
  `tests/project_prompt` (and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer chats
  changed) on the free `claude-cli` backend. Its README also asks for a small
  paid run on the app's default model before a release; propose it with its
  cost.

To tell whether the range caused a failure, run the same test on a build of
the last release's tag. A failure there too is older: report it and let
Kenneth decide. One the range caused is a bug to fix before the release.

## 6. Translations

After the audit and tests, since a fix can add a sentence.

1. Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py` (needs GNU
   gettext and `npm ci` in `AgentUI`). Changed catalogs go in the release
   commit.
2. Translate new entries in JusPrin's own catalogs, `Localization/native/`
   and `Localization/pages/`, as `Localization/README.md` says. Never touch
   upstream's `localization/i18n/` or run `run_gettext`; from `AGENTS.md` and
   the `orca-translations` skill take only the editing rules and glossary.
3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass.
4. Rebuild `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs` for the guide check.
5. Tell Kenneth how many entries are marked `# Needs human review`.

No tool finds a sentence nobody marked for translation; look for one while
reading the range.

## 7. Guide check

Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the step 5 build.

1. Tell Kenneth first: it drives the app on this Mac's screen, and nobody
   should use the computer meanwhile.
2. Add new screens or menu items from the range to the guide before the
   check: it cannot find them, and a page changed after it passes is
   unchecked.
3. Run `<worktree>/scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. The script checks the
   tree it sits in, so the main checkout's copy checks the wrong code. It
   writes `docs/guide/checked-version.txt` when it passes.

## 8. Commit and land

1. The release commit holds `Version.hpp`, the notes, the catalogs, and what
   the guide check changed: `docs/guide/` (pages, `pictures/`,
   `checked-version.txt`) and `AgentUI/src/skills/guide-*/`. Nothing else.
2. If `origin/jusprin-dev` moved past the recorded end of the range, list the
   new commits for Kenneth. With his yes, rebase and redo step 1.4 and
   sections 2 to 7. If he says no, the release waits: your branch cannot
   reach `jusprin-dev` without them.
3. With his yes, push to `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit, then
   `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`. If that pull is refused, stop and
   tell Kenneth without changing the main checkout.
4. With his yes, move `main` to that exact release commit, as a fast
   forward only.

## 9. Start the release workflow

The publisher is the repository variable `JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER`, or
`kennethjiang` when unset; `gh api user -q .login` must print it. This
computer's `gh` token cannot read repository variables or secrets (403), so
the workflow's first job is what reports a wrong publisher or a missing
Sentry secret (`JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`,
`SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`). Only Kenneth can add a secret.

With his yes:

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
```

Keep Mac signing on: Homebrew refuses an unsigned Mac app. Check that the new
`workflow_dispatch` run is on the release commit. If its "Upload to the draft
release" job waits for an approval (the `release` environment can require
one), tell Kenneth. A failed run is reported with its log, never worked
around with a skip box.

The Mac jobs build on GitHub's Macs. If GitHub has no Mac machine for the
repo, they end "cancelled" 15 minutes after they were queued, with no runner
and no steps. Tell Kenneth. With his yes, start the run again on Kenneth's
own Mac (the self-hosted runner, user `jusprin-ci`):

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true -f self_hosted_mac=true
```

## 10. Test the draft

Test the draft's own files: the Mac disk image on this computer, the Windows
installer and the AppImage on their VMs. Install over the previous release,
check that Preferences shows the new version, have one chat and slice, and
check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered. Kenneth signs
in, or you use a test account he names; never type a password. A chat spends
that account's credits.

Sentry must be able to read this release's stacks. Kenneth gives you
`SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT` and a read-only
`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`; set them in the shell only, never in a file. From the
release worktree, on the Mac for the disk image and the unpacked Windows
portable zip (its `JusPrin/` folder), and on the Linux VM for the AppImage
(`--appimage-extract` only works on Linux; that VM needs a checkout of the
release commit and node):

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh verify <file>` on
  the Mac app's `Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer`, Windows' `OrcaSlicer.dll` and
  the AppImage's `squashfs-root/bin/orca-slicer` must print "Sentry holds
  debug information".
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh verify <folder>` on
  the Mac app's `Contents/Resources`, the Windows zip's `JusPrin/resources`
  and `squashfs-root/resources` must say Sentry holds both pages' source
  maps.
- The app cannot cause an error report on purpose, and Help › Report a
  problem opens a GitHub issue, not a Sentry report. If an unexpected error
  happens while testing, send it and check in Sentry, under release
  `JusPrin <version> (OrcaSlicer <SoftFever_VERSION from version.inc>)`, that
  the app's frames show function, file and line. Otherwise say it was not
  done.

`winget_updater.yml`, inherited from OrcaSlicer, would submit the installer
to winget as `SoftFever.OrcaSlicer` on publish. `gh workflow list --all` must
show it `disabled_manually`; if not, tell Kenneth before he publishes.

Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform. He publishes.

## 11. After publishing

- Start the previous release and check that Preferences › Updates offers the
  new one. The update check reads only published releases.
- With Kenneth's yes, reply to and close the issues the release fixes, and
  open a Homebrew cask pull request if JusPrin's cask is in Homebrew
  (`brew info --cask jusprin`).
- In Sentry, a new report's or crash's stack must name the app's functions
  with file and line, and a page error's frames the pages' sources
  (`AgentUI/src/...`, `HomeUI/src/...`). Bare addresses or
  `app:///home/index.html` positions mean a platform's debug files or a map
  are missing: run the verify scripts on that platform's released files.
- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in tsd-enterprise.
- Remove your worktree and branch.

```bash
git grep -n -E '"/(ent|o|accounts|jusprin)/|"/models"|ask_server\("' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*'
```

For example `ask_server("code/confirm", …)` is
`/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/code/confirm`, and the model list is the gateway's
address with its last part replaced by `/models`. A bare GET with no sign-in
or real data is enough: any 4xx answer except 404 means the address is there.

First GET a made-up address such as `/ent/jusprin/v2/no-such-address`: it
must answer 404. In maintenance mode the server answers 200 for every path,
and the check cannot tell anything apart; stop and tell Kenneth.

A missing address means the server change is not deployed. Find it in
tsd-enterprise (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`) and tell Kenneth,
along with any other server behavior the range relies on. Deploying is his
call.

## 4. Error-handling audit

Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
server changes, also audit tsd-enterprise's `web_ent/jusprin/` commits on
`master` since the previous tag's date (that repository has no release tags).
Report the findings and wait for Kenneth to say which must be fixed.

## 5. Tests

Build in your worktree in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
in `AGENTS.md`. Use CMake.app's cmake (Homebrew's fails to find Eigen3), node
on `PATH`, and absolute paths.

The app builds against the main checkout's dependency folder, which may
predate a dependency the range added or changed. Bring it up to date first:

```bash
<worktree>/scripts/deps_current.sh <main checkout>/deps/build/arm64
```

It compares the `deps/` recipe the folder was last built from with the
worktree's, and when they differ it rebuilds the libraries that changed. If
it says the main checkout's recipe differs from the worktree's, the main
checkout is not at the end of the range; stop and tell Kenneth.

```bash
cmake -S <worktree> -B <worktree>/build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<main checkout>/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
cmake --build <worktree>/build/arm64 --config Release --target tests/all jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs -- -j4
ctest --test-dir <worktree>/build/arm64/tests -C Release --output-on-failure -LE RequiresApp
```

`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` takes one path only. `tests/all` builds every test
program, including `shell_integration_harness` for the guide check.
`agent_live_tests` is built but never registered with ctest, since each run
is billed. Also run `npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.

- **Windows and Linux,** on the VMs, from a checkout of the end of the range:
  `build_win.bat -s --run-tests`, and `./build_linux.sh -st` then
  `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release --output-on-failure`, keeping the
  `RequiresApp` tests, which run only on Linux.
- **Prompt suites,** when the range changes text the model reads: run
  `tests/project_prompt` (and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer chats
  changed) on the free `claude-cli` backend. Its README also asks for a small
  paid run on the app's default model before a release; propose it with its
  cost.

To tell whether the range caused a failure, run the same test on a build of
the last release's tag. A failure there too is older: report it and let
Kenneth decide. One the range caused is a bug to fix before the release.

## 6. Translations

After the audit and tests, since a fix can add a sentence.

1. Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py` (needs GNU
   gettext and `npm ci` in `AgentUI`). Changed catalogs go in the release
   commit.
2. Translate new entries in JusPrin's own catalogs, `Localization/native/`
   and `Localization/pages/`, as `Localization/README.md` says. Never touch
   upstream's `localization/i18n/` or run `run_gettext`; from `AGENTS.md` and
   the `orca-translations` skill take only the editing rules and glossary.
3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass.
4. Rebuild `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs` for the guide check.
5. Tell Kenneth how many entries are marked `# Needs human review`.

No tool finds a sentence nobody marked for translation; look for one while
reading the range.

## 7. Guide check

Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the step 5 build.

1. Tell Kenneth first: it drives the app on this Mac's screen, and nobody
   should use the computer meanwhile.
2. Add new screens or menu items from the range to the guide before the
   check: it cannot find them, and a page changed after it passes is
   unchecked.
3. Run `<worktree>/scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. The script checks the
   tree it sits in, so the main checkout's copy checks the wrong code. It
   writes `docs/guide/checked-version.txt` when it passes.

## 8. Commit and land

1. The release commit holds `Version.hpp`, the notes, the catalogs, and what
   the guide check changed: `docs/guide/` (pages, `pictures/`,
   `checked-version.txt`) and `AgentUI/src/skills/guide-*/`. Nothing else.
2. If `origin/jusprin-dev` moved past the recorded end of the range, list the
   new commits for Kenneth. With his yes, rebase and redo step 1.4 and
   sections 2 to 7. If he says no, the release waits: your branch cannot
   reach `jusprin-dev` without them.
3. With his yes, push to `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit, then
   `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`. If that pull is refused, stop and
   tell Kenneth without changing the main checkout.
4. With his yes, move `main` to that exact release commit, as a fast
   forward only.

## 9. Start the release workflow

The publisher is the repository variable `JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER`, or
`kennethjiang` when unset; `gh api user -q .login` must print it. This
computer's `gh` token cannot read repository variables or secrets (403), so
the workflow's first job is what reports a wrong publisher or a missing
Sentry secret (`JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`,
`SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`). Only Kenneth can add a secret.

With his yes:

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
```

Keep Mac signing on: Homebrew refuses an unsigned Mac app. Check that the new
`workflow_dispatch` run is on the release commit. If its "Upload to the draft
release" job waits for an approval (the `release` environment can require
one), tell Kenneth. A failed run is reported with its log, never worked
around with a skip box.

The Mac jobs build on GitHub's Macs. If GitHub has no Mac machine for the
repo, they end "cancelled" 15 minutes after they were queued, with no runner
and no steps. Tell Kenneth. With his yes, start the run again on Kenneth's
own Mac (the self-hosted runner, user `jusprin-ci`):

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true -f self_hosted_mac=true
```

## 10. Test the draft

Test the draft's own files: the Mac disk image on this computer, the Windows
installer and the AppImage on their VMs. Install over the previous release,
check that Preferences shows the new version, have one chat and slice, and
check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered. Kenneth signs
in, or you use a test account he names; never type a password. A chat spends
that account's credits.

Sentry must be able to read this release's stacks. Kenneth gives you
`SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT` and a read-only
`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`; set them in the shell only, never in a file. From the
release worktree, on the Mac for the disk image and the unpacked Windows
portable zip (its `JusPrin/` folder), and on the Linux VM for the AppImage
(`--appimage-extract` only works on Linux; that VM needs a checkout of the
release commit and node):

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh verify <file>` on
  the Mac app's `Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer`, Windows' `OrcaSlicer.dll` and
  the AppImage's `squashfs-root/bin/orca-slicer` must print "Sentry holds
  debug information".
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh verify <folder>` on
  the Mac app's `Contents/Resources`, the Windows zip's `JusPrin/resources`
  and `squashfs-root/resources` must say Sentry holds both pages' source
  maps.
- The app cannot cause an error report on purpose, and Help › Report a
  problem opens a GitHub issue, not a Sentry report. If an unexpected error
  happens while testing, send it and check in Sentry, under release
  `JusPrin <version> (OrcaSlicer <SoftFever_VERSION from version.inc>)`, that
  the app's frames show function, file and line. Otherwise say it was not
  done.

`winget_updater.yml`, inherited from OrcaSlicer, would submit the installer
to winget as `SoftFever.OrcaSlicer` on publish. `gh workflow list --all` must
show it `disabled_manually`; if not, tell Kenneth before he publishes.

Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform. He publishes.

## 11. After publishing

- Start the previous release and check that Preferences › Updates offers the
  new one. The update check reads only published releases.
- With Kenneth's yes, reply to and close the issues the release fixes, and
  open a Homebrew cask pull request if JusPrin's cask is in Homebrew
  (`brew info --cask jusprin`).
- In Sentry, a new report's or crash's stack must name the app's functions
  with file and line, and a page error's frames the pages' sources
  (`AgentUI/src/...`, `HomeUI/src/...`). Bare addresses or
  `app:///home/index.html` positions mean a platform's debug files or a map
  are missing: run the verify scripts on that platform's released files.
- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in tsd-enterprise.
- Remove your worktree and branch.

Yes. The runbook is the `jusprin-release` skill, `.claude/skills/jusprin-release/SKILL.md` on `jusprin-dev`, and it lists every step 2.0.1 went through, from choosing the commit range to the checks after publishing. Since 2.0.1 it has also gained the Mac changes: GitHub's Macs by default, and a box on the release form that moves the Mac jobs to your Mac. I checked it against what actually happened in 2.0.1 and the repository as it is today. One thing would block the next release, and four are smaller gaps.

**Would block the next release**
- **`main` has a commit `jusprin-dev` doesn't:** efa0e6b80f, your README link change from 2026-11-22. It changes one line in `.github/README.md` to link to Obico.
- **Why it blocks:** the skill moves `main` to the release commit as a fast forward only, and that fails while `main` has a commit of its own.
- **The fix:** cherry-pick that commit onto `jusprin-dev` now. It applies cleanly.

**Smaller gaps**
1. **Mac jobs cancelled partway:** the skill says to switch to your Mac only when GitHub gives the Mac jobs no machine for 15 minutes. In 2.0.1, GitHub also cancelled an Apple Silicon build that was already running. Today's 19:28 UTC nightly had both Mac builds cancelled. The skill should treat any cancelled Mac job the same way.
2. **A key printed into a log:** while testing on the Windows VM, a script printed the app's settings file, including the Anthropic key saved there, into the session's log. The skill should say never to print that file.
3. **No chat on Linux:** the skill asks for one chat on every platform. The Linux VM has no AI account or key, so 2.0.1 had no chat there. The skill should either name an account for that VM or say the Linux test is slicing only. That choice is yours.
4. **The Sentry token:** the skill says you hand over a read-only Sentry token for checking the draft. In 2.0.1 the release session used the admin token from your global instructions instead. The skill and practice should agree; which token to use is also your call.

**Already settled since 2.0.1**
- **Signing on GitHub's Macs:** the change to rcodesign works there. The nightly on 2026-11-24 signed the app on a GitHub `macos-15` machine, and Apple's notary service returned "Accepted".
- **Your Mac is ready to take over:** the runner `kenneth-mac-jusprin-ci` is online, and `JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER` is set again.
- **Not yet tried:** the release form's box that moves the Mac jobs to your Mac has never run from `main`. The self-hosted test that signed and notarised ran from a test branch. So the first time the box is used will be in a real release.

My proposal: cherry-pick the README commit onto `jusprin-dev`, and fix gaps 1 and 2 in the skill. That's one or two commits, pushed with your yes. Gaps 3 and 4 need your answer first.

Should I make those fixes now: yes, or not now?

content.text:
I pushed both fixes to `jusprin-dev` and pulled the main checkout. But I got one part wrong: copying the README commit does not unblock the next release.

**What's pushed**
- **e58dbbb7a1:** a cherry-picked copy of your README commit from `main`. `jusprin-dev` now has the same README text.
- **507424cecd:** the skill and the release workflow's header comment now say that a Mac job GitHub cancels partway through gets the same treatment as one that never got a machine. You're told, and with your yes the run starts again on your Mac. The skill also says never to print the app's settings file, only the one setting you need.

**What I got wrong**
- **Why the copy doesn't help:** a cherry-pick copies a change into a new commit. Git can fast-forward `main` to a commit only when that commit's history contains every commit on `main`. Your original README commit, efa0e6b80f, is still only on `main`. So moving `main` to the next release commit still fails. I checked after pushing; I should have checked before proposing.
- **The copy is still useful:** both branches now hold the same file contents. A merge of `main` into `jusprin-dev` produces exactly `jusprin-dev`'s current files, so it can't change any file.

**Decision needed: how `main` gets past its own README commit.** It's your call because you've said you don't want merge commits on `jusprin-dev`. `main` can't be force-pushed, so there are two ways:

1. **One merge commit on `jusprin-dev` that takes in `main`.** It changes no file, and from then on `main` fast-forwards at every release, as the skill expects. The cost is one merge commit in `jusprin-dev`'s history.
2. **Move `main` with a merge commit on `main` at release time.** `jusprin-dev` stays free of merge commits. But `main` then holds a commit `jusprin-dev` lacks again, so the same thing happens at every later release.

My pick is 1: one merge commit once, against a recurring problem every release.

**My proposal (not done):** I'd also add a check to the skill's setup step. If `main` has a commit `jusprin-dev` lacks, the session stops and tells you at the start, instead of finding out when it moves `main`. Separately, editing `main` directly, as with the README change, is what causes this. Whether to forbid that is up to you.

Should I add one merge commit on `jusprin-dev` that takes in `main`, or leave it and merge on `main` at release time instead?
